thread.title: Midday Update: Wall Street Buoyed by Upbeat Inflation, Jobs Data

author: MT Newswires
title: Midday Update: Wall Street Buoyed by Upbeat Inflation, Jobs Data
text:
Shutterstock photo The Dow Jones Industrial Average was trading higher, although off its best levels of the day, as Wall Street digested mixed messages on the US/China trade front with unexpectedly tame inflation data. Led by shares of Dow component stock Apple ( AAPL ) advancers were leading decliners by a ratio of nearly 2-to-1, propping up the blue chip index for a third straight day.
Stocks were kept afloat before the open by overtures from Beijing to restart trade negotiations and a below-consensus 0.2% gain in the nominal consumer price index. Excluding the volatile food and fuel sector, consumer prices were up by just 0.1% in August, half of what was expected. On an annual basis, the CPI was lowered to 2.7% from 2.9% while the core dropped to 2.2% from 2.4%.
Additionally, jobless claims fell to another 49-year low of 204,000 versus expectations for an increase of 7,000 to 210,000.
Early gains were compromised, however, after a tweet from President Donald Trump denied claims made in Wednesday's Wall Street Journal that the US is under pressure to make a deal with Beijing. Trump added that the US "will soon be taking in billions in tariffs," raising odds that $200 billion in new tariffs against Chinese imports will be implemented.
Markets reacted by surrendering nearly half their post-CPI gains as the dollar retreated and the yield on the 10-year Treasury note dropped to 2.95%. The major averages have since regained traction but have yet to return to their opening highs.
European bourses are fractionally lower with Germany's DAX the outlier as gains in automakers, BASF and Infineon Technologies outweighs losses for Merck's ( MRK ) European unit and thyssenkrupp AG.
Thursday was a busy day for European central bankers with the European Central Bank and Bank of England both keeping interest rates unchanged. Stocks across the EU were weighed down by ECB president Mario Draghi's hawkish assessment of inflation targets even as the central bank lowered growth forecasts.
Meanwhile, the head of the Turkish central bank defied President Recep Erdogan and hiked the one-week repo rate by 625 basis points to 24.00% -- almost twice what was expected. Just hours before its announcement to hike rates, Erdogan blamed the central bank for high interest rates and runaway inflation, sending the lira to a four-day low against the dollar. In the wake of the rate hike, the lira soared to a two-week high before reversing some of its gains into the European close.
Crude oil was down $1.65 to $68.72 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.01 to $2.84 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $3.00 to $1,208.30 an ounce, while silver was down $0.04 to $14.25 an ounce. Copper was up $0.01 to $2.69 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was down $2.30 to $14.48 with the United States Natural Gas Fund up 0.39% to $23.30. Among precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 0.07% to $18.04 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.27% to $113.86. The iShares Silver Trust was down 0.07% to $13.38.
